rationale: All four lenses and the standards audit ran and every story criterion passes, but 22 findings block, led by re-applied conversation failures that exhaust the attempt cap in one run, a generation move that skips the file locks, and a rename wait that outlasts the SessionEnd budget. The 30-call reachability budget ran out, so CR-008, CR-009, CR-012, CR-016, CR-018 and CR-020 keep lens evidence and several others are marked unconfirmed; base comparison used read-only git show/diff, outside this agent's Bash allow-list, and that evidence backs the pre-existing calls. Three deferred to code-review-deferred.local.md (conversation payloads have no run window; resumed Codex/Copilot runs can double-count; torn JSONL lines are not repaired); 19 dismissed as noise; no decision_needed items.

findings.title: OpenCode upper bound keyed by directory only
findings.problem: sameTranscriptKeys matches opencode and codemie-code records on working directory alone, so two concurrent records in one directory count as covering the same transcript even when their native sessions differ. Outside a hook process that bound now reaches MetricsWriter.appendDeltas.
findings.impact: After a second record starts, the earlier record's own deltas can be dropped as after_end, and the drop is permanent because the bound stays. Reachability was unconfirmed: the OpenCode adapter's use of the native id was not read within the budget.
findings.recommendation: Key opencode and codemie-code records by their native session id when the record has one, falling back to the directory only when it does not, so a concurrent record over another native session bounds nothing. Add a test with two records in one directory.

findings.title: Kimi records get no upper bound
findings.problem: kimi and kimi-acp reach the default branch of sameTranscriptKeys, which returns no keys, so nextRecordStart gives Kimi no later-record bound. The docs promise this bound through the shared writer.
findings.impact: When a Kimi record resumes a wire transcript another record covers, a late non-hook pass of the earlier record can claim the later record's deltas. Reachability was unconfirmed: whether a Kimi record's correlation names its file was not read.
findings.recommendation: Add kimi and kimi-acp cases keyed by correlation.agentSessionFile, and cover the later-record bound in the Kimi window test.

findings.title: Core and plugins import SSO lock module
findings.problem: architecture.md:152-155 lists Core depending on Plugins and direct Plugin-to-Plugin calls as anti-patterns. run-window.ts and session-generation.ts now import lock code and types from src/providers/plugins/sso, and six agent plugins import appendSessionFile from there. Similar imports exist at base, so this extends a pattern.
findings.impact: The new shared locking contract makes agent core and six agent plugins depend on one provider plugin, against the architecture check in the git-workflow.md review checklist.
findings.recommendation: Move locked-jsonl.ts and the RunWindow and LockBounds types, with the JSONL helpers they need, to a lower layer such as src/agents/core/session or src/utils, and have the callers import them from there.

findings.title: Processor-level lock bounds have no test
findings.problem: regression-gap: the deadline, abort and pid-only liveness are checked on the context and on the writer separately, but no test proves a real processor hands them to the lock wait. Lens evidence: hook-routing-contract mocks processSession, run-window.test.ts asserts only startTime and upperBound, and no test references lockBoundsOf.
findings.impact: Removing the lockBoundsOf spread, or omitting context from an appendSessionFile call, makes a Stop or SessionEnd hook wait the full 10 s and risks a kill mid-pass with tests still green. Consumers: performIncrementalSync at hook.ts:505 and the metrics and conversation processors.
findings.recommendation: Add a processor-level test that holds the metrics and conversation locks, runs a real processor with a short syncDeadlineMs and asserts success:false near the deadline with nothing written; also assert resolveRunWindow returns deadlineMs, signal and pidOnlyLiveness.

findings.title: Generation move skips metrics and conversation locks
findings.problem: The PR requires a session's completed_ rename to take both file locks first, and the locked-jsonl.ts header promises every rename runs under them. moveSetToGeneration(sessionId, '') at hook.ts:1140 and 1416 moves the live set to completed_<id>-<gen> under the reconcile lock only, metrics first and .json last. No test covers it.
findings.impact: While the .json is still live, an appender can create a new live metrics file, and a rewrite that read before the move can rename its result back over the live path. Those lines miss the generation set and are orphaned, which is what this change set out to stop.
findings.recommendation: For the live prefix, take the metrics and conversation locks before moving anything, as renameLiveSet does; a lock not taken moves nothing. Update both hook.ts callers for that failure and add a test that holds the metrics lock and asserts the live file has not moved.

findings.title: Swallowed rename failure reported as closed
findings.problem: renameSessionFiles now records a lock failure as a warning and returns void. closeExhaustedLocally and the exhausted undelivered path then log closed locally or renamed without sending regardless, and an already-aborted parent signal makes acquirePidLock return null before even trying.
findings.impact: The record stays live and keeps its cap slot, which the function's own doc says cannot happen, and the logs are false. Its lines were already marked dropped, so a later pass can deliver a record already reported as dropped.
findings.recommendation: Return whether the set was renamed from renameSessionFiles, log closed locally or renamed only when it was, and do not redeliver a record already marked dropped. Cover the already-aborted signal and held-lock cases.

findings.title: Metrics processors ignore AppendResult
findings.problem: appendDeltas can write fewer deltas than it is given, and when the file is gone it returns written:0 with no flag to separate that from nothing new. Claude, Kimi, Codex, OpenCode and Copilot call sites confirmed here still report deltas.length (or their own batch) as written. Conversation processors got a dropped-write branch; metrics processors did not.
findings.impact: Logs and metadata claim deltas that never reached disk. sync-state-utils.ts:44 accumulates totalDeltas from those counts and persists processed ids, so sync state overstates what was written and drops are hidden.
findings.recommendation: Use AppendResult.written for logs, deltasWritten, recordsProcessed and totalDeltas in every metrics processor, expose the dropped-because-gone case in AppendResult, and add a processor-level test that those fields match the writer after a drop.

findings.title: Codex, Copilot, Pi upper bound untested
findings.problem: regression-gap: per the lens's grep, no Codex, Copilot CLI or Pi test references recordsBeforeMs, nextRecordStart or resolveRunWindow, so their upper bound is never observed. Not re-verified: the review budget ended first.
findings.impact: Dropping the window spread at codex.metrics-processor.ts:103 or copilot-cli.metrics-processor.ts:99, or an upper bound at pi.metrics-processor.ts:509, lets a record count the next record's deltas with tests still green.
findings.recommendation: For Codex, Copilot CLI and Pi, over the real MetricsWriter, assert a delta at or after recordsBeforeMs is absent and an earlier one present, plus a later-record case with no recordsBeforeMs.

findings.title: Gemini window test lacks required cases
findings.problem: The PR lists processor-level run-window tests with both bounds and the hook process for claude, gemini, opencode and kimi. Per the acceptance lens the Gemini file has only the lower bound. Not re-verified: the review budget ended first.
findings.impact: The Gemini upper bound and hook-process behaviour are unguarded at processor level on the agent EPMCDME-16538 targets, while the description says they are covered.
findings.recommendation: Add recordsBeforeMs and hookProcess cases to the Gemini window test, matching the claude, opencode and kimi tests.

findings.title: Kimi resolves window for an empty batch
findings.problem: Kimi calls resolveRunWindow and appendDeltas even when newDeltas is empty, unlike Codex and Copilot, which guard on deltas.length, and Claude, which returns early. That adds a record lookup, a later-record scan and a lock acquisition to a pass with nothing to write.
findings.impact: A missing record or a lock timeout fails a pass that has nothing to do, returning success:false where it previously succeeded. Gemini and Pi call sites have the same shape as far as read; their earlier returns were not checked.
findings.recommendation: Guard the call with newDeltas.length > 0 as Codex and Copilot do, and confirm the same guard exists on the Gemini and Pi paths.

findings.title: Spent budget fails the final write pass
findings.problem: applySessionEndOptions starts the 2 s budget when the context is built, before transcript parsing, and that same deadline bounds the lock wait. acquirePidLock still tries once, so a free lock succeeds, but a lock held at that moment returns null at once and the write throws. Lens evidence: tests cover only a lock held by someone else.
findings.impact: When parsing outlasts the budget and any other writer briefly holds the lock, the SessionEnd final pass fails and the hook continues, so the transcript tail may never be written. Reachability was unconfirmed: what SessionEnd does after a failed pass was not read within the budget.
findings.recommendation: Do not let transcript parsing spend the lock wait of the final pass: give the final SessionEnd write a short lock-wait floor past the sync budget, and add a test with a past deadline and a briefly held lock.

findings.title: Rename bounds forwarding has no test
findings.problem: regression-gap: renameSessionFiles honours its bounds when called directly, but per the lens's grep no test checks that delivery or any reconciliation path passes them. Not re-verified: the review budget ended first.
findings.impact: Reverting any of these calls to renameSessionFiles(id) lets a held lock stall an exit or start pass up to 10 s per lock past its deadline, with tests still green. Consumers: deliverSessionRecord and the exhausted, unqueued and legacy paths in stale-session-reconciliation.ts.
findings.recommendation: Through deliverSessionRecord and the reconciler's exhausted, unqueued and legacy paths, hold the metrics lock with a short deadline and assert a return near the deadline with the set still live, or assert the injected renameSessionFiles received the bounds.

findings.title: Rename lock wait ignores SessionEnd budget
findings.problem: The PR requires the rename to be bounded by a hook's SessionEnd budget. deliverSessionRecord passes only options.deadlineMs, which sessionEndOptions leaves undefined in a hook process without config or CODEMIE_EXIT_DEADLINE_MS, instead of the budgeted deadline every other path gets from applySessionEndOptions.
findings.impact: With a lock held, the rename waits on the abort or up to 10 s per lock, 20 s in total, against a 2 s budget. The agent can kill the hook mid-wait, so the set stays live until a later reconcile pass. Graded critical as a partially met spec requirement; the data survives.
findings.recommendation: Pass a budgeted deadline to renameSessionFiles in a hook process, computed as applySessionEndOptions computes it, so the rename stops within the SessionEnd budget. Add a hook-process test with a held lock.

findings.title: Conversation sync ignores dropped rewrite
findings.problem: Both conversation rewriteSessionFile calls discard the boolean, while the metrics sibling warns. When the file is gone the outcome is lost without a log, and the send loop keeps uploading the remaining payloads.
findings.impact: Later payloads are sent with outcomes recorded nowhere. Reachability was unconfirmed: delivery only renames once nothing is pending, so the likely route is the unlocked generation move in CR-005.
findings.recommendation: Check the boolean from rewriteSessionFile; when the file is gone, stop the send loop as deferred, and log the drop in both call sites as the metrics sync does.

findings.title: Re-applied failures exhaust the sync attempt cap
findings.problem: Every per-payload rewrite re-reads the file and re-applies all of the run's outcomes. applyPayloadOutcome accepts a FAILED record and adds 1 to syncAttempts, so one send's failure is counted again on each later rewrite in the same run. SUCCESS is terminal and unaffected. syncProcessor-merge.test.ts does not assert syncAttempts.
findings.impact: MAX_CONVERSATION_SYNC_ATTEMPTS is 3, so a payload that fails once with two more payloads after it reaches the cap in one run and is never retried. During an outage every payload but the last two is abandoned at once, and conversation history is lost unsent. The base code incremented once per send.
findings.recommendation: Apply each outcome to the file once per send: after a rewrite that persisted, remove its outcomes from runOutcomes and keep only those whose rewrite threw. Add a merge test where one failed payload is followed by two more and assert its syncAttempts is 1.

findings.title: Lower bound can drop a record's own deltas
findings.problem: A delta whose time precedes record.startTime is dropped at debug level only. This assumes a record never starts after its own lines, which is checked nowhere: several fixtures moved startTime back to keep passing. parseDeltaTime also assumes numeric times are epoch milliseconds, and Kimi passes event.time through unconverted.
findings.impact: A record created after its first transcript line, such as a discovered session, or a time in seconds, would lose those deltas with no warning. Reachability was unconfirmed: the review budget ended before Desktop record creation and Kimi's time unit were read.
findings.recommendation: Confirm that every record's startTime precedes its own transcript lines, including discovered Claude Desktop records, and that every numeric delta time is epoch milliseconds (Kimi's event.time passes through unconverted). Log before_start drops at warn level, and normalise or exempt whatever fails either check.

findings.title: Synthesized delta time hits the upper bound
findings.problem: Processors fall back to Date.now() when a line has no time (copilot-cli.metrics-processor.ts:85 and :92, kimi.metrics-processor.ts:216, opencode.metrics-processor.ts:394). The writer judges that synthesized time as real, so reprocessing an earlier record after a later one started puts it past upperBound.
findings.impact: A delta in the record's own window is dropped as after_end, against the writer's rule that a delta with no usable time is kept. Reachability was unconfirmed: how often these lines lack a time was not established.
findings.recommendation: Do not judge a synthesized time: leave the time unusable or mark the delta at the fallback sites, so appendDeltas skips the window check for it, matching the writer's rule that a delta with no usable time is kept.

findings.title: 20 000-line append test misses stated bound
findings.problem: The PR lists a test for one delta at 20 000 lines under 100 ms. Per the acceptance lens the test asserts toBeLessThan(1000), ten times that bound. Not re-verified: the review budget ended first.
findings.impact: The read-per-append cost the bound exists to limit can grow tenfold with the test still green, and the description overstates what is guarded.
findings.recommendation: Align the test and the PR description: assert the stated 100 ms if it is reliable on CI, otherwise correct the description to the bound the test enforces.

findings.title: Lock timeout after upload invites a resend
findings.problem: The final rewrite runs after the server has accepted the batch and has no local catch, and it gains a new failure mode: SessionFileLockTimeoutError after the 10 s budget. Outcomes are held only in memory, so a timeout loses them. When the file is gone, the sync warns and still reports success.
findings.impact: Accepted deltas stay pending on disk and a later pass can send them again, double-counting analytics. It needs the lock held past 10 s, which is uncommon but live; a dead holder with a reused pid in a hook process is one route. Whether the server dedupes resends was not checked.
findings.recommendation: Catch SessionFileLockTimeoutError around the final rewrite and keep the outcome so it is applied on a retry or the next pass, so sent deltas are not sent again. Report the outcome as not persisted rather than as a failed sync.

findings.title: Metrics rewrite failure paths untested
findings.problem: regression-gap: the conversation sync has a rewrite-failure test, but per the lens the metrics sync's file-gone and lock-timeout paths after a completed upload have none; its merge test uses a free lock and a present file. Not re-verified: the review budget ended first.
findings.impact: Changes to either outcome would pass unnoticed, including re-creating a completed file or losing accepted outcomes. Consumers: the session sync during SessionEnd delivery and the Pi tick.
findings.recommendation: With a 200 answer, test (a) the live file removed during the request, asserting no live file is re-created and the returned totals, and (b) the metrics lock held past the wait, asserting the result and that deltas stay pending.

findings.title: New files use deep relative imports
findings.problem: AGENTS.md Common Pitfalls says to avoid deep relative imports and use the @/ alias. locked-jsonl.ts:12-14,21 and run-window.ts:8-10 use paths such as ../../../../../utils/pid-lock.js, while session-generation.ts:6 in the same change uses the alias.
findings.impact: New files introduce an import form the repository's canonical instruction file names as a pitfall; the standards audit reports it as blocking.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite these imports to the @/ alias, for example @/utils/pid-lock.js and @/providers/plugins/sso/session/processors/metrics/MetricsWriter.js.

findings.title: Locked file helpers omit @throws docs
findings.problem: code-quality.md asks for JSDoc with @throws on exported functions. withSessionFile, appendSessionFile and rewriteSessionFile all reach acquireSessionFileLock, which throws SessionFileLockTimeoutError, but their JSDoc has no @throws and their undefined or false results read as the only failure mode.
findings.impact: Callers must handle a lock timeout separately from a dropped write, and the contract hides it; CR-019 is that omission in practice.
findings.recommendation: Add @throws {SessionFileLockTimeoutError} to the JSDoc of withSessionFile, appendSessionFile and rewriteSessionFile.

deferred.title: Conversation payloads have no run window
deferred.problem: Conversation processors over a shared transcript are not bounded, so a record can report turns whose metrics were dropped as another record's.
deferred.preexisting: Conversation processors had no window before this change; it adds the window for metrics only.

deferred.title: Resumed Codex and Copilot runs can double-count
deferred.problem: With no lower bound, a resumed rollout writes earlier calls into the new record, and the recordId dedupe reads only that record's file.
deferred.preexisting: These processors had no lower bound at base; this change keeps that and marks the ceiling in code.

deferred.title: Torn JSONL line is never repaired
deferred.problem: A killed writer's unterminated line absorbs the next append, and strict readJSONL then throws on every later sync and rewrite.
deferred.preexisting: The base appendDelta appended with no newline repair and its readers were just as strict.
